spec_match.rationale: The spec was rewritten (2026-07-27) and the API now lives in the WebRTC Extensions specification (https://w3c.github.io/webrtc-extensions/#diagnostic-logging, the chromestatus spec_link). All four routes and the conformance contract now exercise the rewritten surface: [Exposed=Window] partial interface RTCPeerConnection with static startDiagnosticLogging(optional RTCDiagnosticLoggingOptions options = {}) returning a DOMString synchronously, static stopDiagnosticLogging(), static cancelDiagnosticLogging(), and dictionary RTCDiagnosticLoggingOptions { record<DOMString, DOMString> metadata } — no Navigator binding, no finishDiagnosticLogging, no allowUpload, no [SecureContext]. The conformance suite probes the exact named IDL members with specSection anchors into the canonical spec, and asserts the spec's one TypeError (metadata size > 5 or any key/value length > 100) and its three InvalidStateError contracts (start while a session is active; stop while idle; cancel while idle).

interactive.rationale: Real controls drive the real synchronous methods: logging-lifecycle enables start/stop/cancel only in valid states and logs each synchronous return; bug-report-companion edits metadata rows with a live count and starts a session with that metadata; capability-policy-probe re-runs on demand. On a browser without the implementation the controls are honestly disabled with the exact enable steps (runtime feature + enterprise policy), and a browser that still exposes the pre-rewrite navigator.rtc surface is named as legacy rather than counted as present. No faked session is ever shown.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The feature index cards and lede describe exactly what the concepts deliver — the three RTCPeerConnection statics, synchronous returns, metadata limits as a TypeError, and the runtime-feature + enterprise-policy gate — and the enabling-it section now records the current ChromeStatus state (Proposed, desktop 156, is_released false, no origin trial) plus the verified Chrome 154 divergence.

edge_cases.rationale: Covers the honest negative branches: unbound static surface (disabled controls + flag note + legacy-surface note), per-surface method absence in the probe table, the conformance suite's three InvalidStateError contracts and both metadata-limit arms (>5 entries and a >100-char value) asserting TypeError, and a start() that throws InvalidStateError surfacing in the UI ('err' status) rather than being swallowed.

references.rationale: The feature index cites chromestatus.com/feature/5091582546149376, the canonical WebRTC Extensions spec section, the WICG mirror, the explainer, w3c/webrtc-extensions#124, and the Chromium tracking bug (crbug.com/481412281). The conformance specSections anchor into the canonical spec. The old copy's 'origin trial 150-155' claim was removed because the 2026-09-30 chromestatus record no longer lists a trial (origintrial: false).

conformance.rationale: Immutable suite rewritten to the current surface: 9 assertions (three typeof checks on the RTCPeerConnection statics, the removal of the Navigator binding, the synchronous session-ID return, the three InvalidStateError contracts, and the metadata TypeError). Verified executing live in real Chrome 154.0.8037.97: 1 pass / 8 fail / 0 blocked — the 8 fails are the honest api-surface-absent-in-this-chrome verdicts (Chrome 154 does not implement the statics) and the single pass is legacy-navigator-rtc-removed. Against a spec-faithful injected implementation the same in-page suite reports 9/9 pass, so the assertions are shown to be satisfiable rather than vacuously red.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Driven in headless Chrome 154.0.8037.97 via the repository's own CDP driver (scripts/lib/cdp.mjs) — chrome-devtools-mcp is not configured on this VM. Evidence in ~/fleet-evidence/chrome-platform-showcase/p4m/ (48/48 driver checks, results.json). PART A (real Chrome, no injection): all four routes render the honest unsupported path — start disabled, flag note shown, honest status text — with zero console errors (a-*.png). PART B (a spec-faithful mock injected before page scripts, because no Chrome build here implements the surface): logging-lifecycle start() returns a UUID synchronously, stop() finalises, cancel() discards, and an InvalidStateError from start() surfaces in the 'err' status; bug-report-companion stamps the session ID onto the report and shows the spec TypeError for 6 metadata entries; capability-policy-probe reports all three statics present; the in-page conformance panel is 9/9 pass (b-*.png). The mock proves the demo code, not Chrome's implementation — browser-availability.json records the real Chrome probe: with default flags the statics and navigator.rtc are all undefined, and with --enable-blink-features=RTCDiagnosticLogging the statics remain undefined while the pre-rewrite navigator.rtc.{start,finish,cancel}DiagnosticLogging appear.

telemetry_health.rationale: The concepts emit showcaseTelemetry.assert events per branch with the renamed events (rtc-start-returns-id, rtc-stop, rtc-cancel, rtc-start-with-metadata, rtc-metadata-limit-enforced, rtc-probe-consistent, rtc-probe-ran); the server injects /public/demo-telemetry.js when serving the pages (routes/release.ts). All four routes ran with zero console errors and zero failed requests during the drive.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout; the removed allowUpload checkbox leaves the shared button background+color pairs and focus-visible styling intact; the metadata count-note keeps its aria-live warning. python3 .claude/audit-demos.py --strict reports the same four raw-colour warnings as origin/main (none new to this feature).

accessibility.rationale: role=status/aria-live on the status lines and call log, aria-live=polite on the session ID and the metadata count-note, aria-labels on metadata inputs and remove buttons, and a probe table with an aria-label and scope=col headers — all preserved across the rewrite. The static accessibility audit reports no new issues versus origin/main, and the metadata editor remains fully keyboard-operable.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: The four routes were loaded at 390×844 and 360×740 in real Chrome: document.documentElement.scrollWidth equals window.innerWidth on every page (the long RTCPeerConnection method names and the enterprise-policy token wrap via overflow-wrap), with zero console errors (c-index-390.png).

openQuestions.title: Re-verify Chrome 156, when the static surface is expected to ship
openQuestions.detail: As of ChromeStatus updated 2026-09-30 the feature is 'Proposed' at desktop milestone 156 with is_released false and origintrial false. Chrome 154.0.8037.97 ships the PRE-rewrite navigator.rtc surface behind --enable-blink-features=RTCDiagnosticLogging and does not expose the RTCPeerConnection statics at all. When a Chrome build implements the statics, re-run the conformance suite live (expect 9/9 on a real implementation), confirm the error names (TypeError vs any Chromium RangeError divergence), and move the enabling-it copy off 'Proposed'.

openQuestions.title: Re-verify the spec's canonical location and the discard method name
openQuestions.detail: The conformance specUrl now points at the WebRTC Extensions spec (chromestatus spec_link). The WICG mirror still carries the same IDL but its table of contents labels the third method discardDiagnosticLogging() while the normative IDL and prose say cancelDiagnosticLogging(); the demos use the IDL name. If the spec settles on a different name, update both the routes and the conformance contract.

guidanceConsulted.query: labelling metadata inputs and announcing synchronous validation errors without changing the editor layout
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Associate labels with inputs, use aria-live for dynamic error announcements, and never rely on placeholder-only naming.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: the metadata count-note (a dynamic over-limit warning) keeps aria-live=polite so the TypeError path is announced; the per-row key/value inputs keep their aria-labels. No layout change was needed for the copy migration.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: live count-note updates during metadata add in the p4m drive; b-bugreport-typerror.png

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible live regions for synchronous probe and lifecycle results after button activation
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Announce dynamic state through live regions tied to the activating control; keep semantic tables and named controls.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Verified applied: status lines and the call log are live regions, the probe table is aria-labelled with scoped headers, and the legacy-surface row is announced as text rather than colour-only.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: capability-policy-probe and logging-lifecycle a/b screenshots; static audit reports no new issues

summary: Rewritten-surface migration of the WebRTC Diagnostic Logging family: all four routes and the conformance contract moved from the pre-rewrite navigator.rtc/startDiagnosticLogging/finishDiagnosticLogging/allowUpload surface to the current WebRTC Extensions surface — static RTCPeerConnection.startDiagnosticLogging()/stopDiagnosticLogging()/cancelDiagnosticLogging(), synchronous returns, metadata-only options, one TypeError and three InvalidStateError contracts. Verified against the primary spec and in real headless Chrome 154.0.8037.97: the static surface is absent (so the demos show the honest disabled path and the in-page conformance suite reports 1 pass / 8 fail), while the same suite reports 9/9 against a spec-faithful injected implementation that was used to drive the lifecycle, metadata-limit and probe control flow. Added a focused contract test wired into deno task check (22 fails red-first on origin/main, 0 after), regenerated demo-index.json, and updated the critique rubric and open questions to the current ChromeStatus state.
